messages:
mira: Quick RFC follow-up on the 'payload tethering' sketch I posted earlier — want to make sure we agree on operator idempotency boundaries before I update the draft.
jonathan: +1, can you summarize the tethering bit for folks who didn't read the wall of text? :sweat_smile:
mira: TL;DR: instead of embedding large model blobs in the staged bundle we deliver a small, signed tether manifest that references chunked assets. Operator pulls blobs lazily via a seeded transfer or an offline sidecar. Activation happens only after a separate signed activation token exchange. Goal: faster bundle distribution, smaller deltas, and safer activation.
alex: I like the distribution angle. My concern is the activation race and partial-apply surface. If operator crashes after some blobs landed but before activation, how do we guarantee a safe rollback? Operator idempotency needs a clear transact model.
priya: Right — we should define three idempotent operations: plan (download/verify), stage (place staged symlink + metadata), activate (atomic switch + post-activate probe). Each op must be repeatable and have an explicit outcome enum: PENDING, STAGED, ACTIVATED, ROLLBACK_PENDING, ROLLED_BACK.
mira: Exactly. Proposal: manifest holds a per-asset content-hash and a lease token. Download writes to tmp/<lease-id>/<chunk> and reports checksums; once all chunks verified we write a staged-manifest file with the lease token. Activation exchanges the lease for a signed activation stamp from the control-plane (or an on-prem signing escrow), which is then validated locally before symlink swap.
jonathan: How long are leases valid? Need to avoid leaving half-staged content lying around indefinitely and also avoid killing long-running downloads behind flaky networks.
priya: Default lease TTL = 24h; operator garbage-collector reclaims expired leases after N backoff retries. GC should only remove content that's not referenced by any staged-manifest. We should expose a --grace-period flag for sensitive regimens (airgapped customers may want longer retention).
alex: Two practical edge-cases: 1) operator upgrade while there are existing leases and 2) operator idempotency across restart where activation stamp was applied but post-activate probes haven't completed. For (1) we ensure forward-compatible on-disk layout: store op-version in staged-manifest, and new operator can either adopt or migrate leases atomically.
mira: For (2) activation should record an activation intent before swap and write an activation journal entry which the agent can replay if interrupted. Journal replay logic: if intent present + activation-stamp present -> run post-activate probe; if intent present + no stamp -> attempt to reacquire stamp from control-plane fallback (or roll back after X tries).
priya: We need a small API surface for the control-plane to support this flow: 1) mint_lease(manifest_id, assets[]) -> lease_token 2) confirm_stage(lease_token, checksums[]) -> stage_ack 3) request_activation(lease_token) -> activation_stamp (signed) 4) revoke_lease(lease_token) -> revoke_ack.
jonathan: That API looks fine. Security note: activation_stamp must include asset root hash + operator instance id + monotonic nonce; signed by customer's KMS or Redwood escrow depending on deployment. If escrow used, include attestation bits.
alex: Observability: expose per-lease lifecycle metrics (lease_created, downloaded_bytes, stage_success, activation_success, lease_gc). Add a per-asset verification histogram so we can track failure modes (corruption vs missing chunk).
mira: UX for operators: minimal CLI commands: `ri operator fetch --manifest m.json`, `ri operator stage --lease L`, `ri operator activate --lease L`. We should allow a single `fetch --activate` mode that does plan->stage->activate but only for non-critical installs.
priya: Backpressure and network-smoothing: propose a bounded parallel download queue with adaptive concurrency based on success rate and latency. Also allow optional sidecar handshake where a USB/side-transfer signals chunk provenance (airgap transfer scenario).
jonathan: One more: rollback semantics if activation fails after partial swap. We should support two rollback modes: fast-revert (atomic symlink flip back) and fail-open (leave staged available and mark route pinned to previous assets). Recommend default fast-revert and a customer-configurable policy.
alex: +1 to default fast-revert. Also add a 'dry-run-activation' probe that simulates activation path without flipping symlinks for preflight checks.
mira: Cool. I'll add these sections: lease lifecycle, on-disk layout, activation journal, control-plane API, GC policy, operator CLI, metrics. Anyone object to me adding a short pseudocode snippet for journal replay?
priya: Go for it.
mira: ```
# journal replay pseudocode
if journal.contains('activation_intent'):
  if disk.has('activation_stamp'):
    run_post_activate_probe()
    journal.clear('activation_intent')
  else:
    if controlplane.request_activation(lease) succeeds:
      write_activation_stamp()
      run_post_activate_probe()
      journal.clear('activation_intent')
    else:
      if attempts > RETRY_LIMIT:
        trigger_rollback()
```
jonathan: That helps. One nit: include a short mechanism to surface manual operator intervention hooks (e.g., operator can `ri operator rescue --lease` to fetch logs and optionally force-accept activation stamp). We need audit events for every step.
mira: Will do. I'll update RFC and ping the thread. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment note: RFC doc updated at https://docs.internal/repo/rfcs/payload-tethering.md — mira, please ping #eng-releases when ready for spec review.
mira: pinged. Thanks!
